    Filter Rare Species from Community Data

    FilterRare.Rd

    Removes rare species from community data based on occurrence frequency and/or total abundance thresholds. Useful for reducing noise and focusing analyses on more common, ecologically relevant species.

    FilterRare(DF, shape = "w", mocc = 0.05, mab = 1, method = "and")

    Arguments

    DF

    A data.frame containing community data. The first column should contain station names (if shape = "w") or species names (if shape = "l").

    shape

    Data format specification (default = "w"):

    • "w" - Wide format: stations in rows, species in columns (first column = station names) (default)

    • "l" - Long format: species in rows, stations in columns (first column = species names)

    mocc

    Minimum proportion of samples where species must occur (default = 0.05, i.e., 5\ are removed. Set to 0 to disable occurrence filtering.

    mab

    Minimum total abundance across all samples (default = 1). Species with total abundance below this threshold are removed. Set to 0 to disable abundance filtering.

    method

    Filtering method (default = "and"):

    • "and" - Species must meet BOTH criteria (occurrence AND abundance)

    • "or" - Species must meet EITHER criterion (occurrence OR abundance)

    Value

    A list with four elements:

    • filtered_data - Data frame with rare species removed, same format as input (stations as rows if shape="w")

    • removed_species - Character vector of removed species names

    • kept_species - Character vector of retained species names

    • summary - Data frame with filtering statistics including original species count, removed count, retained count, and criteria used

    Details

    Rare species are common in ecological datasets but can:

    • Add noise to multivariate analyses (ordination, clustering)

    • Inflate apparent beta diversity

    • Be artifacts of sampling error or misidentification

    • Have disproportionate influence in some diversity indices

    Filtering Criteria:

    Occurrence (mocc):

    Proportion of samples where species is present (abundance > 0).

    Example: mocc = 0.05 with 100 samples means species must

occur in at least 5 samples.



\strong{Use when:} Focusing on widespread species, reducing singleton effects,

preparing data for presence-absence analyses

    Abundance (mab):

    Total number of individuals across all samples.

    Example: mab = 10 means species must have at least 10 total

individuals across all samples combined.



\strong{Use when:} Removing species with very few individuals that may be

sampling artifacts, focusing on numerically important species

    Method "and" (default):

    Species must satisfy BOTH occurrence AND abundance thresholds. More conservative - removes more species.

    \strong{Use when:} You want only well-represented species

    Method "or":

    Species must satisfy EITHER occurrence OR abundance threshold. More permissive - removes fewer species.

    \strong{Use when:} You want to keep species that are either widespread

(even if not abundant) OR abundant (even if localized)

    Recommended Thresholds:

    • Exploratory analysis: mocc = 0.05 (5\ mab = 5-10

    • Ordination (NMDS, PCA): mocc = 0.10 (10\ mab = 10

    • Indicator species: mocc = 0.20 (20\ mab = 20

    • Diversity indices: Use with caution - may bias richness

    Important Considerations:

    • Filtering affects richness-based diversity indices (reduce values)

    • May remove ecologically important but rare species (endangered, specialists)

    • Should be justified and reported in methods

    • Consider ecological context - a "rare" predator may be ecologically important

    • For beta diversity, filtering can reduce artifactual dissimilarity

    References

    Cao, Y., Williams, D.D. & Larsen, D.P. (2002). Comparison of ecological communities: the problem of sample representativeness. Ecological Monographs, 72(1), 41-56. https://doi.org/10.1890/0012-9615(2002)072 (0041:COECTP)2.0.CO;2

    Poos, M.S. & Jackson, D.A. (2012). Addressing the removal of rare species in multivariate bioassessments: the impact of methodological choices. Ecological Indicators, 18, 82-90. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolind.2011.10.008

    Marchant, R. (2002). Do rare species have any place in multivariate analysis for bioassessment? Journal of the North American Benthological Society, 21(2), 311-313.

    Legendre, P. & Legendre, L. (2012). Numerical Ecology (3rd ed.). Elsevier.

    See also

    PreData for data format preparation

    Examples

    # Example 1: Basic filtering - wide format
community_data <- data.frame(
  Station = paste0("St", 1:20),
  Common_sp1 = rpois(20, 50),      # Common: occurs in all stations
  Rare_sp1 = c(rep(0, 18), 3, 2),  # Rare: only 2 stations, low abundance
  Common_sp2 = rpois(20, 30),      # Common
  Rare_sp2 = c(1, rep(0, 19))      # Very rare: only 1 station
)

# Filter: must occur in 10% of samples AND have 10+ total individuals
result <- FilterRare(community_data, shape = "w",
                     mocc = 0.10, mab = 10)
result$summary
#>                     Metric Value
#> 1   Original species count     4
#> 2          Species removed     2
#> 3         Species retained     2
#> 4       Removal percentage    50
#> 5 Min occurrence threshold   0.1
#> 6  Min abundance threshold    10
#> 7            Filter method   and
result$removed_species
#> [1] "Rare_sp1" "Rare_sp2"

# Example 2: Long format
community_long <- data.frame(
  Species = c("Capitella", "Owenia", "Nephtys", "Rare_sp"),
  St1 = c(45, 23, 12, 0),
  St2 = c(50, 18, 15, 1),
  St3 = c(48, 25, 10, 0)
)
result2 <- FilterRare(community_long, shape = "l",
                      mocc = 0.30, mab = 5)

# Example 3: Only occurrence-based filtering
result3 <- FilterRare(community_data, shape = "w",
                      mocc = 0.15, mab = 0)

# Example 4: Only abundance-based filtering
result4 <- FilterRare(community_data, shape = "w",
                      mocc = 0, mab = 20)

# Example 5: Permissive filtering (OR method)
result5 <- FilterRare(community_data, shape = "w",
                      mocc = 0.25, mab = 50,
                      method = "or")
